Meanwhile docs/operations/runbook.md recommends running them against a live deployment: "Re-scan (Home store strip, or `npm run rescan`)" and deployment.md §First run "docker compose exec app npm run seed".
gaps.partial:
The claim is accurate, but here is the precise partial picture, because two mitigations exist and one of them makes the seed case worse than the rescan case.

WHAT EXISTS
- The lock itself is complete and well-built: `app/server/db/data-root-lock.server.ts` — O_EXCL create of `<dataRoot>/state/writer.lock`, evidence-based staleness (bootId → hostname → pid liveness), `VIBERR_FORCE_DATA_ROOT_LOCK=1` takeover, release on exit and on the signal path (`sse-broker.server.ts:371`), plus the F18-5 ownership guard re-verifying inode+bootId every 20 s and exiting 1 on a `stolen` verdict.
- It is armed on exactly one path: `bootServer()` → `takeDataRootWriterLock(env)` (`boot.server.ts:205`, acquiring at :161), which `entry.server.tsx` awaits at module scope. So server-vs-server exclusion works, and the holder is observable at `GET /resources/health` (`lock: {pid, hostname, startedAt}`) and on the Home store strip.
- A lock-safe rescan path DOES exist in-product and runs inside the locked server process: `app/routes/_index.tsx:105` (`intent="rescan"`) and `:139` (`intent="rebuild-projections"`, admin-only), plus per-project `app/routes/project.board.tsx:79-87` (`rescan-project`). So for rescan the CLI is a convenience duplicate of a safe path.

WHAT IS ABSENT
- No CLI acquires the lock, and none checks whether another process holds it. All three maintenance entrypoints (`npm run rescan`, `npm run seed`, `npm run seed:demo`) open the same `state/projection.sqlite` and write it with no coordination at all.
- There is no in-app equivalent of the product seed. `runSeed()` and `seedOrgResources()` (org KBs, skills, domain allowlist) have no route caller anywhere in `app/` — grep finds callers only in `scripts/seed.ts`, `scripts/seed-demo.ts` and tests. `bootServer()` seeds only `seedDefaultAgentAssets()` and `seedInitialAdmin()`. So the org-resource baseline is reachable ONLY through the unlocked CLI.
- The F18-5 guard does NOT catch this case. `resetStore()` (`seed.server.ts:104-124`) removes `projects/`, `agents/profiles/` and runtime transcript dirs — it never touches `state/`, so the lock file survives, ownership still verifies as `held`, and the running server keeps writing while the CLI writes the same WAL. The guard only fires when someone wipes `state/` directly, which is a different failure.
- Nothing in the docs flags the hazard, and two docs actively steer the operator into it while the app is up: `docs/operations/deployment.md` §First run recommends `docker compose exec app npm run seed` immediately after `docker compose up -d`, and `docs/operations/runbook.md:30` and `:54` offer `npm run rescan` as a live remedy ("Fix the file on disk … or run `npm run rescan`"). Meanwhile `deployment.md:220-239` states the invariant as absolute — "One app process per data root, EVER" — with no carve-out or caveat for the CLIs. The README quickstart is the only safe ordering (seed before `npm run dev`), and that is incidental rather than stated.

Net: the invariant is enforced against a second *server*, not against a second *writer*. The smallest closing change is a shared helper the three scripts call — acquire the lock (no `force`, `releaseOnExit: true`) and exit non-zero with the existing `DataRootLockedError.message`, which already names the holder and both remedies — plus a doc correction so `deployment.md` and `runbook.md` stop recommending a live `exec`.

gaps.title: Raw run transcripts and SDK session homes on disk are never pruned
gaps.what_is_absent: There is no retention for the on-disk `runtimes/<backend>/<runId>.jsonl` transcripts or for the Claude/Codex session state under `runtimes/claude-home` / `runtimes/codex-home`. The retention pass covers SQLite tables only; the workspace reclaim covers task clones only. No pass, no age window, no size cap, and no mention of the growth in the runbook's growth section.
gaps.why_it_matters: An operator reading the runbook concludes that run logs are bounded to 30 days — that is true of the projected rows, and false of the files that back them. On a team running agents daily the .jsonl set becomes the largest unbounded item in the data root after workspaces, it is inside every backup, and (for codex-home) may sit next to a live credential. There is also a quiet asymmetry: after 30 days the run console is empty while the raw transcript export still resolves.
gaps.intent_basis: docs/operations/runbook.md §Retention & growth frames itself as the complete answer to "what grows and what bounds it", explicitly calling out the one SQLite table with no retention (provenance) and the one disk item that is reclaimed (workspaces).
gaps.evidence_of_absence: app/server/db/retention.server.ts touches exactly three tables: run_log_lines, audit_events, notifications. app/server/tasks/workspace-retention.server.ts removes only `projects/<slug>/tasks/<KEY>/workspace`. One .jsonl file is created per run (app/server/runtimes/run-store.server.ts:356 `rawLogPath`, with the docblock "One file per run, always") and appended by `appendRawLine`; the only code that deletes them is the destructive `npm run seed -- --reset` (app/server/seed/seed.server.ts:98-99). docs/operations/runbook.md notes "Raw run logs are append-only under $VIBERR_DATA_ROOT/runtimes/<backend>/" but never says they are unpruned, and its §Retention & growth disk subsection covers only task workspaces.
gaps.partial:
The claim holds, with three refinements worth carrying into the gap list.

(1) What DOES bound this stream, partially: the SQLite projection of the same run output, run_log_lines, is deleted after 30 days (RUN_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS, app/server/db/retention.server.ts:21,64-68). So the log console is bounded, but the on-disk raw truth of the same run is not — after 30 days the DB rows are gone and the .jsonl remains forever, which also inverts the usual relationship (the "canonical raw truth" outlives the thing that reads it, and becomes unreadable through the product: app/routes/resources.run-log.ts reads the DB projection, not the file). There is also no per-run cap: appendRawLine (run-store.server.ts:374-385) appends unconditionally, and run-sink.server.ts has no line or byte ceiling.

(2) An orphaning path the claim missed: deleteProject (app/features/project-settings/settings-actions.server.ts:805-816) removes projects/<slug> and the project's notifications, then rebuilds projections — but never touches the runs' .jsonl files. Deleting a project therefore leaves its transcripts on disk permanently with no remaining reader at all (the agent_runs rows that named them are gone). Same for archived/deleted tasks.

(3) Session homes: runtimes/claude-home (claude-config.server.ts:31; sessions at $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<cwd-as-dashes>/<sid>.jsonl, env.server.ts:109-112) and runtimes/codex-home (codex-config.server.ts:67; sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ts>-<sid>.jsonl, session-export.server.ts:13-14) are created by DATA_ROOT_SUBDIRS (app/server/files/file-store-root.server.ts:28-33) and never swept by Viberr. codex-home is a single shared app-owned run home (prepareCodexHome, codex-config.server.ts:121-160), so its sessions/ tree accumulates one rollout file per run indefinitely. The only partial mitigation is provider-side and is treated in code as a HAZARD rather than a policy: agent-reply.server.ts:241-248 notes "Claude Code's ~30-day retention" as a cause of dead session ids (P13-D-2), and there is no Codex equivalent — a wiped $CODEX_HOME/sessions is described as a manual act.

Docs gap is real too: docs/operations/runbook.md:110 states raw run logs are append-only under $VIBERR_DATA_ROOT/runtimes/<backend>/ without saying they are unbounded, and §Retention & growth (131-187) presents itself as the complete answer — it names provenance as "the one table with no retention" and task workspaces as the one disk item reclaimed, so a reader correctly concludes nothing else on disk grows. docs/operations/deployment.md:163-169 mentions runtimes/ only as backup scope.

gaps.title: Encryption-key rotation can never be finished: no re-encrypt pass and no count of secrets still on a retired key
gaps.what_is_absent: Rotation of VIBERR_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY is implemented as a lazy re-seal on read, but there is no batch re-encryption command, no report of how many stored secrets still open only under a retired key, and no signal that convergence is complete. There is also no rotation procedure in docs/operations at all.
gaps.why_it_matters: "Drop the old key once every secret has been re-saved" is an instruction the operator cannot execute, because nothing tells them when that is true. The dormant cases are exactly the risky ones: a PAT on a project nobody has touched this quarter, an MCP server credential used by one agent. Remove the retired key and those silently fail later — the org resources path degrades an authenticated MCP server to unauthenticated. Keep it forever and the rotation never actually retires the compromised key, which is the entire point of rotating.
gaps.intent_basis: app/server/secrets/secret-box.server.ts §KEY ROTATION (A9) states rotation should "converge on the new key with no migration and no downtime" and ends with the operator instruction to drop the retired key; .env.example documents VIBERR_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS as a bounded "rotation window".
gaps.evidence_of_absence: /Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/app/server/secrets/secret-box.server.ts implements `openSecretRotating` + `previousSecretKeys` and documents the design: "a box that opened under a retired key is RE-SEALED in place by its caller… Once nothing opens under a retired key any more, drop it from the env." The only two callers are app/server/secrets/pat-store.server.ts:209 and app/server/org/resources.server.ts:620 — both re-seal on read, so a PAT or MCP credential that is never read is never migrated. No script, route, or admin action enumerates or re-seals stored boxes (grep for `staleKey` outside tests returns only those two sites). docs/operations/deployment.md:29 states the opposite of what ships: "losing or rotating it makes existing encrypted tokens undecryptable (users must re-add PATs)" — the operator-facing doc does not know the rotation window exists.
gaps.partial:
WHAT EXISTS: the read-side rotation window is real and proven. app/server/secrets/secret-box.server.ts:55-72 `previousSecretKeys()` parses VIBERR_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS (comma-separated, newest first, 32-byte-validated, malformed entries skipped in silence so key material never reaches an error message); :88-101 `openSecretRotating()` tries the current key then each retired key and returns {plaintext, staleKey}. Both sealed stores re-seal on read: pat-store.server.ts:204-222 rewrites github_pats.encrypted_token; org/resources.server.ts:600-640 rewrites the MCP credential and logs "re-sealed an MCP credential under the current encryption key". Those are the only two sealed stores — `sealSecret(` has six non-test call sites, all belonging to them. Tests assert the behaviour: secret-box.server.test.ts:88-143 (describe "secret-box key rotation (A9)") and specialist-mcp.server.test.ts:184-213. .env.example:18-26 documents the window correctly, including "Remove it once every stored secret has been re-saved." A per-row failure pill exists at app/features/org-settings/resource-rows.tsx:214-221 ("auth: unreadable — rotate the encryption key or re-enter the credential").

WHAT IS MISSING: (1) No batch re-encryption command, script, route, or admin action — nothing iterates github_pats or the MCP resource rows. A PAT or MCP credential on a dormant project is never read, therefore never migrated, and rotation never converges. (2) No count or report of how many stored boxes still open only under a retired key — `staleKey` is never aggregated, there is no boot-time scan, and the org-settings pill shows the *unreadable* state (no key opens it) per row, not the stale-but-openable state, and gives no total. (3) No convergence signal, so nothing ever tells the operator it is safe to drop VIBERR_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS — precisely the action the module's own comment ends by instructing. (4) No rotation procedure in docs/operations at all: runbook.md's "GitHub / PAT issues" section covers scope/expiry/revocation only, and deployment.md:29-30 actively contradicts what ships by telling operators that rotating the key forces users to re-add PATs.

ONE DETAIL THE CLAIMANT MISSED, which strengthens the gap: org/resources.server.ts:670-685 `openedForNewRow` deliberately does not re-seal ("there is nothing to lazily re-seal into"), so that path reads a box under a retired key and leaves it retired — a second way a secret can stay stale indefinitely even when it IS read.

gaps.title: No recovery path for a corrupted or badly hand-edited canonical task file
gaps.what_is_absent: Files are canonical and hand-editable by design, but there is no file history, no previous-version copy, no undo, no in-app view of the raw task.md, and the data root is not version-controlled. Diagnostics report that a file is broken without showing it or offering a revert.
gaps.why_it_matters: The runbook's whole diagnostics story terminates in "fix the file" with no way to know what it used to say. A truncated write from an editor, a botched sed, or an agent-adjacent hand-edit that drops a `## Timeline` section is unrecoverable except from a backup — and the backup capability is itself missing (gap 2). This is the Murat journey's blast radius: he is the person called in when a task looks inconsistent, and the app can tell him the file is wrong but cannot show it to him or restore it.
gaps.intent_basis: PRD Journey 4 (Murat investigates a continuity failure) rests on the canonical task file being trustworthy enough to reconstruct from; INTENT.md and the architecture treat markdown files as the durable source of truth that outlives the 90-day audit window.
gaps.evidence_of_absence: Writes are atomic (app/server/files/atomic-file.server.ts: tmp write + renameSync) but keep no prior copy — no `.bak`, no revision directory. `DATA_ROOT_SUBDIRS` in app/server/files/file-store-root.server.ts is projects/, agents/, kb/, skills/, runtimes/, state/ — no history/ or versions/ directory. Grep across app/features/task-detail for a raw-file/`task.md` viewer returns nothing (the KB editor is the only in-app file editor). docs/operations/runbook.md §Diagnostics offers exactly one remedy: "Fix the file on disk → the watcher re-projects within ~1 s".
gaps.partial:
WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT (the claim's core, verified):
1. No prior-version copy of any canonical file. app/server/files/atomic-file.server.ts writes tmp + `renameSync`; the old bytes are gone at rename. Same for project.md (project-writer.server.ts) and agent profiles.
2. No history/versions directory in the store (DATA_ROOT_SUBDIRS, file-store-root.server.ts:23-35), and the data root is not a git repo — no code path runs git against it.
3. No in-app raw view or edit of `projects/**/task.md`. app/routes.ts has no such route; the store browser (app/features/kb-browser/store-browser.tsx) is org-settings-only and scoped to kb/ + skills/.
4. No undo/revert/repair action anywhere — grep of task-actions.server.ts, e2e/ and qa/ for repair|undo|revert finds only the comment-composer undo and unrelated "silently reverted" comments.
5. FileDiagnostic (app/schemas/file-diagnostics.ts) carries severity/code/path/message/hardStop — no line number and no excerpt field.

WHAT DOES EXIST, and materially narrows the claim:
a) Ops-level backup/restore IS a documented product procedure, not a void: docs/operations/deployment.md §"Persistence, backup & restore" (~:160-205) — snapshot the whole data root including the `projection.sqlite-wal`/`-shm` sidecars; "Restore = drop the directory back". runbook.md:189-192 points there and warns that a `projects/`-only restore re-mints user ids and orphans every membership/owner. So the recovery path that exists is whole-data-root restore from an external backup; what is missing is anything finer-grained (one file, one edit) and anything in-app.
b) The app never loses the human's hand-edited content on top of a bad edit. Parsing is tolerant and never drops an entity (file-diagnostics.ts header), and both writers preserve unknown data: task-file.server.ts:40 "Unknown `## Sections` are preserved verbatim (round-trip safe)" and task-writer.server.ts header "Unknown frontmatter fields and unknown `## Sections` survive every write."
c) Diagnostics do more than say "broken": each finding carries a machine code and the offending field path, is persisted into the projection (rebuilder.server.ts:124 writes hard_stop; task-query.server.ts:33,128-133 reads it), floors readiness per diagnostics-policy.server.ts (hardStop→blocked "file not trusted", error→inconsistency_risk_detected, warning→input_required), renders in DiagnosticsPanel (task-main-sections.tsx:42-73), and lands in Activity→Audit. Several parsers embed the offending text: task-file.server.ts:113-114 quotes the malformed timeline heading (`slice(0,80)`), :129 the unparseable timestamp, :292 and frontmatter.server.ts:65 the YAML error's first line.
d) The task page DOES tell you which file to open — task-main-sections.tsx:177 renders `task.filePath` (a real store-relative path, e.g. `projects/viberr-core/tasks/VIB-142/task.md`, per ruling 3).
e) Derived-state recovery is first-class: Home's store strip has "Re-scan store" and an admin-only, confirmed "Rebuild projections…" (home-sections.tsx:535-641; rebuild.server.ts described as the hammer for a corrupted projection DB), plus `npm run rescan` and a reconciling rescan at boot. That recovers the projection from the files — it cannot recover a file.

PRECISE GAP STATEMENT: the file layer has integrity detection (diagnostics + readiness floor + audit) and coarse ops restore, but no reversibility. Once a human or agent writes a bad `task.md`, the only routes back are (i) hand-repair on disk guided by a code/path/message with no line number and no raw view in the app, or (ii) restoring the entire data root from an external snapshot, which also rolls back the SQLite side (users, sessions, PATs, audit, notifications) — there is no way to restore one file. PRD Journey 4 (Murat reconstructing a continuity failure from the canonical file) has no in-product answer to "what did this file say before the edit that broke it".

NOTE ON SCOPE: I found no numbered ruling and no PRD amendment that deliberately cuts file versioning — grep of docs/architecture/decisions.md, prd.md, architecture.md and INTENT.md for version control|versioning|file history|undo|hand-edit returns only architecture.md:818 (projection.sqlite must never be hand-edited, and is not a cache). So this is not a recorded deliberate cut; it appears simply never to have been specified.

gaps.title: The deployment operator is not a persona the product serves — every operational act is docs plus curl
gaps.what_is_absent: There is no in-app operations surface. The only admin operational UI is the StoreStrip footer (re-scan, rebuild projections, writer-lock holder). Health, watcher liveness, backend credential state, retention results, data-root size, migration state and boot integrity exist only as a stdout log line or an unauthenticated JSON endpoint an operator must curl.
gaps.why_it_matters: On a small self-hosting team the operator is the same person as Arda or Elif, working in the browser. Today every operational question — is the watcher alive, did Codex lose its credential, when did retention last run, how big is the data root, which build is this — requires leaving the app for a shell. That is a defensible choice for a single-node monolith, but it is currently an unstated one, which is why the individually small gaps above (version, disk, alerting, rotation state) have no natural home to land in.
gaps.intent_basis: PRD §Journeys defines the personas the product serves and includes no deployment operator; docs/operations/{runbook,deployment}.md carry the entire operational contract as prose.
gaps.evidence_of_absence: app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:533-601 is the complete admin ops UI. The health payload (app/routes/resources.health.ts) is consumed by no page in app/. Boot integrity (app/server/boot.server.ts `logBootIntegrity`) and retention results (app/server/db/retention.server.ts "retention pass complete") go to the logger only. The PRD's four journeys are Arda supervising, Arda intervening, Elif configuring a project (labelled "admin / operations", but scoped to workflow/RBAC/agent policy), and Murat troubleshooting a task — none is the person who runs the container.
gaps.owner_question: Should there be a single admin-only System/Operations page (health, watcher, backends, lock holder, version, data-root size, last retention pass) — or is the deliberate position that operations stay in docs, logs and the shell, and the missing pieces above should be added there instead?
gaps.partial:
WHAT ALREADY EXISTS IN-APP (so "every operational act is docs plus curl" is wrong):

1. **Backend credential state is in-app and actionable — this is the strongest refutation.** `backendCredentialHealth()` (`/Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/app/server/runtimes/runtime-registry.server.ts:336`) returns `{backend, available, verification: "credential"|"file"|"presence"|"none", detail}` where `detail` is a remediation sentence naming the exact env var (e.g. "No Claude credential is configured. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, or opt in to a logged-in `claude` CLI with VIBERR_CLAUDE_USE_CLI_AUTH=1", and a Codex equivalent naming the missing `auth.json` path). It is loaded by `/Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/app/routes/project.agents.tsx:47-53` and rendered on the Agents roster as `BackendChip` → an amber "not configured" badge with `detail` as its title (`/Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/app/features/agents/agents-page.tsx:56-116`), plus `ActiveBadge`'s `unusable` state so an idle-but-uncredentialed profile can't read as healthy. The same fact disables unavailable backends in the task run picker (`app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx:592,700`). The deployer's core question — "did the Claude/Codex credential reach the container?" — is answered in the UI, richer than the health JSON's `real|unavailable`, not only by curl. Its docblock even cites this as the F16 gap that was closed.

2. GitHub credential health: `validationState` (`valid` / `not validated` / `validation failed`) plus per-scope verified/missing chips from a real PAT probe (`app/features/org-settings/connections-panel.tsx:15-18,236-302`); per-project live repository-access probe and sync freshness with an explicit stale-vs-never-synced distinction, R17-5 (`app/features/github/github-view.tsx:55-81,439-469`).

3. MCP server health with a Test-connection action and an honest "not health-checked yet" state (`app/features/org-settings/resource-rows.tsx:193,212`; `testMcpServer` in `app/server/org/resources.server.ts`).

4. Re-scan exists at TWO levels, not one: the admin StoreStrip (`app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:533-601`) and a per-project maintainer-gated Re-scan on the board (`app/routes/project.board.tsx:79-89` intent `rescan`, button `app/features/board/board-page.tsx:927`). Plus `npm run rescan` (package.json:17) — a script, not curl.

5. Data root is surfaced to admins: `app/routes/_index.tsx:62` (`storeRoot`) renders in the new-project modal as the literal path being created (`app/features/home/new-project-modal.tsx:368`). A real on-disk browser with per-file sizes exists over the store (`app/features/kb-browser/store-browser.tsx:419`).

6. Liveness of the client stream has a pill with retry (`app/features/shell/topbar.tsx:163-172`); task-level diagnostics + project Activity → Audit log cover the runbook's "a task looks wrong" path.

WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT (verified by grep, no reader anywhere in app/):

- **`/resources/health` is consumed by no page.** Its only readers are the Docker healthcheck, `playwright.config.ts:9`, README and tests. Confirmed by grepping every `*.ts`/`*.tsx` for `resources/health`.
- **Watcher / kbWatcher liveness has no UI at all.** Grepping `watcher` across every `.tsx` in app/ returns exactly one hit, a code comment in `app/routes/_index.tsx:121`. A dead store watcher — which the health probe reports truthfully as a REAL dead handle — is invisible to every human in the product.
- **Boot integrity and migration state are logger-only.** `logBootIntegrity` (`app/server/boot.server.ts:44-73`, called at `:309`) emits dataRoot, `dataRootDirsOk`/`missingDirs`, `migrationsApplied`, `latestMigration`, projection and user counts to stdout. Nothing in app/ reads `schema_migrations`.
- **Retention results are logger-only.** `app/server/db/retention.server.ts:99` — `logger.info("retention pass complete", result)`. Same for the workspace reclaim pass (`reclaimed finished task workspaces`, count + MB) in `app/server/tasks/workspace-retention.server.ts`, called from boot.
- **No data-root or disk-usage view.** The store browser's sizes cover kb/ and skills/ only — `resolveStoreTarget` handles `kind === "kb" | "skill"` and returns null otherwise (`app/server/org/resources.server.ts:1654-1681`). Nothing reports the 11–16 MB-per-task workspace clones the runbook itself flags as the real growth surface (`docs/operations/runbook.md:171-188`), nor `provenance`, the one unretained table the runbook says grows unbounded.
- **Org/auth-scoped audit has no in-app reader.** The audit panel is project-scoped (`app/features/activity/activity-page.tsx:71`); `auth.login.*`, `org.user.*`, `github.pat.*`, `org.connection.token_replaced` rows are written and then deleted at 90 days without ever being displayable (consistent with INTENT.md §6 divergence 12, which makes the retention deliberate but says nothing about the missing reader).

PRECISE FRAMING FOR THE OWNER: the gap is not "no operational UI" — credential, connection and reconciliation state are all in-app and were deliberately built there across passes 16–18. The gap is narrower and more defensible: **there is no surface for the facts that are already computed at boot or on a timer and thrown away into stdout** — watcher liveness, migration/boot integrity, retention and workspace-reclaim outcomes, and store footprint. Everything needed already exists server-side; the health probe assembles four of these fields today for an unauthenticated consumer while no authenticated admin can see them.

gaps.title: Only an agent can produce the verdict that unblocks acceptance — a human review counts for nothing
gaps.what_is_absent: Any way for a HUMAN to record the approving verdict that R15-1's gate requires. `report-validation-verdict` is declared agent-only (`app/shared/capabilities.ts:86`, audience `["agent"]`), verdicts are written solely from the agent outcome envelope, and there is no approve / request-changes control anywhere in the UI. A human reviewer's own GitHub PR approval is fetched but deliberately inert: `deriveReviewState` (`app/server/github/pr-linker.server.ts:137`) carries a docstring saying "this is a status pill, not the merge gate", and `verdictGateReason` (`app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts:4997`) never consults it.
gaps.why_it_matters: On a small team the tech lead usually IS the reviewer. Today his only paths are (a) engage an AI reviewer he does not need, or (b) be a project admin and force-accept — which writes an override row asserting he bypassed a gate he actually satisfied, polluting exactly the audit trail FR33 exists for. FR37 literally names the task owner "reviewer + acceptance authority", so the product's own vocabulary promises something the verdict machinery cannot express, and a contributor-owner cannot force-accept at all.
gaps.intent_basis: FR37 ("one human task owner = reviewer + acceptance authority") pulls against ruling 20 / R15-1 ("acceptance requires a verdict", where a verdict means a verdict-capable agent engagement). Ruling 19's principle — "a chip is evidence, never a pseudo-check" — argues a real human approval on the PR is better evidence than an agent's.
gaps.evidence_of_absence: `verdictGateReason` returns "…has no approving verdict yet — run a review for a verdict, or an admin can force-accept" whenever `deriveValidation(fm)` is not `healthy`; `deriveValidation` (`app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts:579-608`) reaches `healthy` only when every profileId in `requiredReviewers(fm)` has an `approve` verdict. Grep for a human verdict writer or an approve control in `app/features` returns nothing (only a comment in `board-page.tsx:341`). `force-accept-completion` is project-admin only (`app/shared/rbac.ts:83`) and audits as `task.acceptance.forced` naming the gate bypassed (live: USE-CASES #27).
gaps.owner_question: Should a human be able to record the approving verdict — either as a first-class action on the task, or by admitting the PR's own GitHub approval from a project member — so that human review stops having to masquerade as an admin override?
gaps.partial: PARTIAL, and the scope matters. What EXISTS is the human DECISION: `accept-completion` behind a confirm dialog naming what will merge (accept-confirm.tsx), with only a human acceptance triggering the real merge (R16-6); admin-only audited `force-accept-completion` (rbac.ts:83 → `task.acceptance.forced` naming the bypassed gate); packet options "Send back for another attempt" and "Redirect with sharper guidance" (task-actions.server.ts:1687-1697) to route work back; and the ability to engage/run a reviewer agent (intents assign-reviewer / run-reviewer). A human REJECTION is also fully load-bearing: closing the PR unmerged on GitHub is ingested as a terminal fact that outranks every process gate (R16-3, `closedPrBlockedReason`, task-actions.server.ts:4451ff). What does NOT exist is any way for a human to record the APPROVING verdict `deriveValidation` requires — no capability, no RBAC action, no route intent, no UI control, and no schema field to hold a human reviewer's identity. So the real shape of the gap is an asymmetry: a human's disapproval binds the gate, a human's approval is inert (their GitHub PR approval is explicitly "a status pill, not the merge gate" per the deriveReviewState docstring in app/server/github/pr-linker.server.ts). The sharpest consequence, verified in code and by test: `deriveValidation` (app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts:579-608) returns `changed` when `requiredReviewers` is empty but a `workRevision` exists, so a project running NO verdict-capable agent can never accept delivered work except via admin force-accept — meaning every acceptance in such a project is permanently audited as a bypass of a gate no one could have satisfied.

gaps.title: Per-run autonomy is chosen from a dropdown that overrides project policy in both directions, unclamped and unaudited
gaps.what_is_absent: Any clamp, disclosure or audit of the autonomy a run is launched at. `resolveOperatorAuthority` takes `overrides.autonomy` and returns it verbatim (`app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts:266`: `overrides.autonomy ?? readAutonomy(definition)`) — the deployed operator profile's configured autonomy is never a ceiling. `gate()` (:284-304) then promotes every `recommend` capability to `direct` under full autonomy (only `completion-for-acceptance` is exempt).
gaps.why_it_matters: Two costs, opposite directions. A Strict/Balanced project's maintainer can silently run one turn at full autonomy, converting every recommend-mode capability into direct execution, with no confirm, no distinct audit row, and only a toast naming it — which the UX contract says must never be the sole record of a consequential event. Conversely an Autonomous project runs Supervised by default whenever a human presses the button, so the configured policy the Policy page describes is not what actually runs.
gaps.intent_basis: Ruling 2 makes agent capability policy a per-project configured system, and the Policy page presents operator autonomy as project configuration (`app/features/policy/policy-page.tsx:514`). Ruling 20/FR27's rationale — "an admin who configured `recommend` expecting a human gate must never get a silent agent-close" (quoted at operator-actions.server.ts:296-298) — is applied to acceptance only; every other recommend capability is promoted freely.
gaps.evidence_of_absence: The task page's operator control is a bare two-option select defaulting to `supervised` (`app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx:608,626-635`), and the route always forwards whatever it says (`app/routes/project.task.tsx:724-735`) — so the profile's configured autonomy is effectively never used from that button. The schedule form is the same (`app/features/task-detail/task-main-sections.tsx:439-442`), and `scheduleTaskAction` validates only `dueAt` and the terminal stage (`app/server/tasks/schedule.server.ts:143-160`). `runtime.run.started` audit details record `backend`, `role`, `kind`, `resumed` — not autonomy (`app/server/runtimes/run-service.server.ts:394-409`).
gaps.owner_question: Should the per-run autonomy selector be clamped to the deployed operator profile's configured autonomy (raising it becoming an audited, disclosed escalation), or is a free per-run choice the intended escape hatch?
gaps.partial:
WHAT EXISTS (the claim overstates "any clamp, disclosure or audit"):

1. The specific clamp intent demands DOES exist. `completion-for-acceptance` is declared `promotable: false` in the catalog (`app/shared/capabilities.ts:52`, comment at :44-51) and `gate()` hard-exempts it (`app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts:295-299`). This is exactly PRD FR27 / owner ruling Q1 — "Raising autonomy alone never confers this" (`planning/planning-artifacts/prd.md:245`, INTENT.md:135, decisions.md:99). So the single consequential capability is clamped by design. `merge-pull-request` / `transition-to-done` / `change-project-policy` are `human`+non-promotable too, and `gate()` returns deny for `off`/`human` at any autonomy — asserted at `operator-actions.server.test.ts:352` ("even full autonomy cannot override an `off` capability"). Full autonomy therefore only promotes `recommend`→`direct` for assignment, packets, typed events, stage-transitions and `deliver-review-pr`; it cannot reach Done or a merge.

2. Per-run autonomy override is deliberate, specified, and tested — not an oversight. PRD FR39 (`prd.md:238`) states a schedule "carries the backend and autonomy level chosen at schedule time"; INTENT.md:47 defines the operator as running "at `supervised` or `full` autonomy" (a per-run property). `app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.test.ts:143` asserts `resolveOperatorAuthority` "honors autonomy override".

3. Disclosure at launch exists (ephemeral): `app/routes/project.task.tsx:751-752` toasts "Operator running · Claude Code · full autonomy" / "Operator queued … · full autonomy".

4. Scheduled autonomy is durably disclosed AND audited: written into the canonical `schedules[]` entry in `task.md` (`app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts:222-224`), named in a timeline event ("… (full · Claude Code)", `app/server/tasks/schedule.server.ts:181`), rendered in the schedules list as "operator · {autonomy} · Claude Code" (`app/features/task-detail/task-main-sections.tsx:373`), and recorded in the `task.schedule.created` audit details (`schedule.server.ts:194`). UC-18 in NOTES.md:117 verified this live.

5. Autonomy IS audited at the one consequential boundary: `task.operator.accepted_completion` details carry `{ autonomy: "full", toStage }` (`operator-actions.server.ts:2657`), and the completion timeline event says "Operator accepted completion under **full-autonomy** policy" (`:2643-2646`; no-change variant at `app/server/tasks/no-change-completion.server.ts:309`). Policy and Review pages disclose the exception in copy (`app/features/policy/policy-page.tsx:514`, `app/features/review/review-page.tsx:169`). The operator's own prompt carries a "# Live authority / Autonomy: **full**" block (`app/server/runtimes/operator-run.server.ts:2076-2081`).

WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT:

a. No ceiling. `resolveOperatorAuthority` returns `overrides.autonomy ?? readAutonomy(definition)` verbatim (`operator-actions.server.ts:266`); the confirmed claim. Grepping the whole tree for `maxAutonomy`, `autonomyCeiling`, `allowFullAutonomy`, `autonomyMax` returns zero hits in app/, docs/ and planning/. The project schema carries only the operator's own `autonomy` (`app/schemas/project-file.schema.ts:104-106`) — nothing models it as a bound. Any `run-agents` role (maintainer+) can launch at `full` on a project whose operator is configured `supervised`. Bounded blast radius (point 1 above), but real: stage transitions and `deliver-review-pr` configured `recommend` execute directly.

b. No audit of the autonomy a run was launched at. `runtime.run.started` details are `{threadId, backend, role, kind, resumed}` (+`failedUnavailable`) — `app/server/runtimes/run-service.server.ts:394-409`; `run-service.server.ts` contains no occurrence of "autonomy" at all. The `agent_runs` table has no autonomy column (`db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql:259`). The activity-feed row renders only "opened the operator runtime session" (`app/server/projections/activity-feed.server.ts:257-259`). Once the toast fades, nothing persists whether a completed run was supervised or full — so PRD journey 4 (Murat investigating after the fact) cannot answer "why did the operator move that stage itself?".

c. No divergence disclosure at the control. The backend select defaults to the profile's configured backend (P11-76, `app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx:583-607`); the autonomy select is a hardcoded `useState("supervised")` (`:608`) that never reads the deployment's configured value, is not labelled an override, and shows nothing when it differs from project configuration. Same for the schedule form (`task-main-sections.tsx:440`, `defaultValue="supervised"`). Net effect confirmed: a project configured `full` silently runs supervised from that button, and a project configured `supervised` can silently run full — with no "differs from project policy" signal at the control, in the timeline, or in the audit log.

d. `scheduleTaskAction` validates only `dueAt` and terminal stage (`schedule.server.ts:143-160`); the autonomy of an unattended future run is recorded but never checked against project configuration.

Net: the acceptance clamp exists and is exactly what the rulings require; a general autonomy ceiling, a run-start autonomy audit, and any override/divergence disclosure do not.

gaps.title: Agent spend is recorded per run and shown nowhere, and nothing bounds unattended work
gaps.what_is_absent: Any surfaced or enforceable notion of cost. `total_cost_usd` is captured and persisted per run, but no page renders it, there is no per-task/project/org total, and no budget, run-count or concurrency ceiling exists anywhere.
gaps.why_it_matters: FR39 is described in INTENT.md as "the one capability that lets an agent act unwatched", and full autonomy plus a scheduled re-run plus the R18-2 delivery re-queue can chain real provider work with nobody present. The team is paying for that and the app already knows the number — it just never shows it. For a self-hosted box, unbounded concurrent Codex/Claude processes is also a reliability question, not only a billing one.
gaps.intent_basis: Ruling 11 ("tokens only from real usage envelopes") shows cost data was deliberately made trustworthy but was never given a home; FR39's own framing flags unwatched action as the exceptional case. Throughput/governance-load analytics is Phase 2, so an org-wide cost dashboard is explicitly post-MVP — a per-task cost line and a ceiling are not the same feature.
gaps.evidence_of_absence: Stored: `app/server/runtimes/run-store.server.ts:39,82,100,165` and `run-sink.server.ts:259-289`. Rendered: grep for `totalCostUsd` / `costUsd` across `app/features` returns nothing; the runs panel shows tokens only (`app/features/runtime/runs-panels.tsx:218`). No `budget` / `maxRuns` / `concurrency` limit exists — the only loop bound is `OPERATOR_TRANSITION_CHAIN_CAP = 8` (`task-actions.server.ts:135`), which caps consecutive operator-authored transitions, not runs or spend, and the operator lease is per task so N tasks means N concurrent provider processes.
gaps.owner_question: Is agent spend deliberately out of V1 scope, or should the cost Viberr already records become a visible per-task/per-project number — and should a project be able to set a ceiling that stops unattended work rather than only bounding transition chains?
gaps.partial:
WHAT EXISTS (the claim is wrong here):

1. Cost IS rendered today, on one surface. The Claude `result` envelope's projected console line is built as `success · ${turns} turns · ${durSec}s · $${cost.toFixed(2)}` at /Users/akinozer/projects/viberr/app/server/runtimes/wire-format.server.ts:141-142, with the full breakdown (`dur, api, turns, cost, in, cached, out`) carried in `display.stats` (:145-158, typed at app/features/runtime/runtime-types.ts:47-58). That display object is persisted into `run_log_lines.display_json` (app/server/runtimes/run-sink.server.ts:264-280) and rendered verbatim by the logs panel — `{entry.line.display.text}` at app/features/runtime/runs-panels.tsx:614; `result` is not a telemetry tag so it is never collapsed (app/features/runtime/log-noise.ts:25-36). The `{ } raw` toggle additionally prints `total_cost_usd` from the stored envelope.

   Verified LIVE against docker-data/state/projection.sqlite:
     `{"t":"11:28:04","ev":"result","tag":"result","text":"success · 11 turns · 150s · $0.15","stats":{...,"cost":0.1509733,...}}`
   The grep for `totalCostUsd`/`costUsd` in app/features returned nothing because the value reaches the UI inside a pre-rendered string, not as a named field.

2. Unattended work IS bounded — by six things, not one:
   - `OPERATOR_TRANSITION_CHAIN_CAP = 8` (app/server/tasks/task-actions.server.ts:135) — the only one the claim names.
   - `OPERATOR_REACT_DEPTH_CAP = 4` (same file, :122,:152) — bounds operator re-entry depth.
   - `VIBERR_CLAUDE_MAX_TURNS`, default 2000 (app/server/runtimes/claude-runtime.server.ts:386,:577); hitting it emits an explicit `run·error·max_turns` line (:751-753). The code itself calls it "A runaway guard, NOT a work budget" (:574).
   - Claude idle timeout `VIBERR_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 15 min (claude-runtime.server.ts:165-170).
   - Codex idle timeout `VIBERR_CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 15 min, owner ruling A8 (codex-runtime.server.ts:300-310,:415-447).
   - Delivering single-flight: one in-flight delivering run per task, refused by name (specialist-run.server.ts:375-387) and enforced by the DB index `idx_agent_runs__one_delivering`. Plus `MAX_SCHEDULE_RETRIES = 3` (schedule.server.ts:277) and the operator repo-view per-run call budget (4 lists / 20 reads / 24k chars).
   "Nothing bounds unattended work" is therefore wrong; what is missing is a MONEY or RUN-COUNT bound, not any bound.

WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT (the finding, narrowed):

a. No aggregation of cost at any scope. `total_cost_usd` has no reader in the app: the only occurrences outside tests are the write path (app/server/runtimes/run-store.server.ts:39,82,100,165) and the projection (wire-format.server.ts:135). `getRun`/`listRuns` do `SELECT *` (run-store.server.ts:180,190) so the column is fetched, but nothing sums it — no per-task, per-project, per-agent-profile, or per-org total exists. Live DB: 76 runs, $8.61 total, computed by me with sqlite3, not by the product.

b. No labeled cost surface. The live run strip shows exactly four cells — Elapsed / Turns / Tokens / Runtime (runs-panels.tsx:205-222) — with no cost cell. app/routes.ts has no usage/cost/billing route. Cost appears only as an unlabeled fragment of one transcript line behind "View logs".

c. Codex runs have no cost at all. The Codex SDK emits none — `expect(facts.costUsd).toBeUndefined()` (wire-format.server.test.ts:85-91). Live: all 5 codex runs have `total_cost_usd` NULL; 69/71 Claude runs have a value. So even the transcript surface is Claude-only.

d. The one visible surface expires before the stored number does. `RUN_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS = 30` deletes `run_log_lines` on every boot (app/server/db/retention.server.ts:21,65-66) while `agent_runs` rows are untouched — after 30 days the money figure still sits in the DB with no way to see it.

e. No ceiling of any kind on spend or run count. No `budget`/`maxRuns`/`spendLimit` column in db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql, no such field in project or org settings, no such env var. The org-wide cost dashboard is fairly read as Phase 2 (prd.md:190 "analytics on throughput, governance load, and task health"), but a per-task cost line and a spend/run ceiling are separate features and neither is scoped anywhere.

f. Nothing in the intent corpus mentions cost as a product concern: grep for cost/budget/spend/billing across planning/planning-artifacts/prd.md and planning/discovery-2026-08-06-pass19/INTENT.md returns zero hits, and decisions.md's only cost hits are unrelated prose. So this is not a deliberate cut recorded anywhere — it is unaddressed.

SUGGESTED REFRAMING of the finding: not "cost is shown nowhere and nothing is bounded", but "cost is captured per run and surfaced only as an unlabeled fragment of a Claude transcript line that is deleted after 30 days; it is never aggregated to a task, project, or org, is absent entirely for Codex, and no spend or run-count ceiling exists — the existing bounds (turn cap, two idle timeouts, chain/react caps, delivering single-flight) are runaway guards, which the code says explicitly, not budgets."
